title: Statistical properties of quadrangular surfaces
authors: Hrant Topchyan, Rudik Badalyan, Ara Sedrakyan
abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of random quadrangular surfaces generated by different randomization procedures: the Gruzberg-Klümper-Nuding-Sedrakyan (GKNS) construction, and two newly introduced generalizations of dynamical triangulations (DT), dynamical (DQ) and general quadrangulations (GQ). We formulate these surfaces within a unified graph-theoretic framework and establish the relationships between the elementary operations defining the different ensembles. For GKNS surfaces, we demonstrate that the construction is equivalent to two mutually constrained percolation processes and determine the associated critical point and critical exponents, revealing deviations from ordinary percolation. For DQ and GQ, we analyze the underlying Markov chains and determine the scaling of mixing and relaxation times. We further analyze all three ensembles through their degree distributions, degree correlations, distance statistics, and Hausdorff dimensions. While DQ exhibits exponentially decaying degree distributions and geometric properties similar to DT, GKNS and GQ display broad, scale-free degree distributions. Moreover, GKNS surfaces possess an asymptotic Hausdorff dimension $Δ_H\approx 2$, whereas DQ and GQ approach $Δ_H\approx 4$, similarly to DT. This indicates that DQ is compatible with the universal behavior of DT, while GKNS and GQ define distinct classes of random geometry, implying a different underlying measure in the space of random surfaces and a possible geometric framework for a new class of noncritical string theories.
summary: This paper compares the statistical geometries of three types of random quadrangular surfaces (GKNS, DQ, GQ) used as models for 2D quantum gravity. By analyzing observables like Hausdorff dimension and degree distributions, the authors demonstrate that GKNS defines a unique universality class distinct from standard triangulations. This suggests new geometric frameworks applicable to non-critical string theories.
main_problem: The study investigates and compares the statistical geometric properties of three different ensembles of random quadrangular surfaces: GKNS, Dynamical Quadrangulations (DQ), and General Quadrangulations (GQ).
main_result: The analysis reveals that while DQ and GQ approach a Hausdorff dimension similar to standard DT ($\Delta_H \approx 4$), the GKNS ensemble defines a distinct class of random geometry with $\Delta_H \approx 2$.
method: The authors use a unified graph-theoretic framework, analyzing underlying Markov chains, degree distributions, and distance statistics for all three ensembles.
model_or_system: The system consists of discrete surfaces modeled as quadrangulations (random graphs), which are used to study concepts related to 2D quantum gravity and non-critical string theories. The specific models include the GKNS construction and generalizations of dynamical triangulations (DQ/GQ).
key_observables:
Degree distributions (scale-free vs. exponential decay), Hausdorff dimension ($\Delta_H$), critical exponents ($
u, \gamma$), and scaling relations for surface area versus diameter.
important_parameters: The critical probability ($p_0$) for the GKNS percolation process; the size/area ($S$); and the crossover diameter ($D_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the different randomization procedures (GKNS, DQ, GQ) define distinct but related ensembles of random surfaces.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate surface representations derived from a disordered potential (ES, SN, dSN, PL), show surface modifications via specific operations ($A_\eta$, $R$), and depict scaling relationships between area and diameter for the different models.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a unified graph-theoretic framework to relate elementary operations defining the ensembles. It then analyzes percolation properties (GKNS) and Markov chain convergence/scaling laws (DQ/GQ), culminating in a comparison of geometric observables like Hausdorff dimension across all three classes.
why_interesting: While focused on geometry, the rigorous statistical mechanics approach to characterizing universality classes and critical phenomena in random manifolds has parallels with understanding phase transitions or emergent order in complex quantum many-body systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: The representations of random surfaces. A disordered potential (color map: increasing from blue to brown), with marked extrema points (Sp: green, Min: blue, Max: red) and connections Sp-Min (blue lines), Sp-Max (red lines), Min-Max with a common Sp (yellow lines) and Sp-Sp with a common Min/Max (black arrows). The extrema surface (ES): all extrema as nodes, Sp-Min and Sp-Max lines as links, and faces Sp-Min-Sp-Max; the scattering network (SN): Sp-s as nodes, Sp-Sp lines as links, and Min-s/Max-s corresponding to the faces; the dual of SN (dSN), Min-s and Max-s as nodes, Min-Max lines as links, as Sp-s representing the faces; the percolation lattice (PL): Min-s as nodes, polylines...
FIG. 2: The surface modifications in different representations. The notations are the same as in Fig.1. The line segment fans represent an arbitrary continuation of the surface.
FIG. 3: The decompositions of operations A†, R and AA† in dSN representation. Colors are there for the ease of following the procedure and don’t represent anything.

FIG. 4: The bipartite (red and blue points) dSN surface (black lines), the diagonals η0 (dashed) and η′ (solid) (red lines), the corresponding opposites ¯η0 and ¯η′ (blue lines) and an example of a chain {¯ηi} continuously connecting them (green lines).

FIG. 5: A GKNS realization on a regular network in the PL representation. The Min (blue nodes and lines) and Max (red nodes and lines) partitions, with the occupied (highlighted) links being depicted thickened. Green dots portray the Sp-s of the initial ES representation.
